title: Costed Cache Policy Syndicator: automated recommendations & safe apply workflow
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Goals: build an automated recommendation service that synthesizes request traces, batching characteristics, and KV/prefix access patterns to output cost-aware caching suggestions (TTL profiles, cache key normalization, and batching hints) plus a guarded apply/rollback workflow. This ticket scopes the core engine, offline hit-rate modeling module, and a staged safe-apply orchestration for production rollout.

Background: we repeatedly see suboptimal caching configs across tenants that increase token cost and GPU compute. Existing docs capture manual heuristics but operators need an automated, auditable recommender that can propose TTL ladders, prefix bucketing, and key-shaping rules with expected hit-rate and cost delta. The recommender must surface uncertainty, recommended confidence, and an action plan for risk-limited staged deploys and automatic rollbacks.

Scope (this ticket):
- Design and implement the offline hit-rate estimator and delta-cost simulator that consumes sampled request telemetry and prefix histograms.
- Implement a candidate generator that proposes (1) per-prefix TTL tiers, (2) cache key normalization transforms (tokenization/truncation/coalescing), and (3) batching window suggestions and batch size caps.
- Provide a safety orchestration harness: shadow dry-run, small-percentage canaries, monitor-based auto-revert.
- Produce API and CLI for operators to preview recommendation reports and opt into staged apply.

Out of scope: live retraining of hit model, UI console integration (separate PM ticket), multi-tenant quota enforcement layer.
acceptance_criteria: Hit-rate estimator produces stable predictions on held-out traces with MAE <= 6% across three sample tenants
Simulator can project per-minute cost delta and token-saved estimate for a proposed TTL ladder
Candidate generator emits at least three ranked policy options per prefix with confidence score and estimated cost/latency impact
Safety harness supports shadow apply, 1% canary, 10% ramp with automated rollback based on defined triggers
End-to-end documentation and a CLI 'preview' command that returns JSON report and explicit rollback plan
rollout_plan: Sprint 1: instrument offline trace extractor and prototype hit-rate model; validate on two tenants' week-long traces (dev cluster)
Sprint 2: build candidate generator and cost simulator; generate proposals and run offline counterfactuals via shadow replay
Sprint 3: implement safety harness + canary controller; integrate health checkers and rollback enforcer
Sprint 4: internal dogfood on non-critical namespace; iterate on thresholds and false-positive suppression
Production: gated rollout with opt-in via CLI and Ops playbook; initial scope limited to low-risk prefix buckets
safety_triggers: observed hit-rate drop > 8% absolute compared to baseline over 10 minutes
predicted latency increase > 20ms p50 during canary window
token cost reduction projection deviates from observed by > 30% for 15 minutes
error rate increase > 0.5% absolute or 3x baseline in canary region
any SLO alert firing for affected route
